title: Single KYC Onboarding and Refresh

slot.brief: Application type: Single. Write this reusable task for Single only; set Application type to Single.

S1.scope: All individual single-applicant accounts undergoing initial onboarding or periodic refresh across applicable jurisdictions, applying relevant jurisdictional compliance standards, organizational charter mandates, and policy versions effective on the application or review date.
S1.title: Single KYC Onboarding and Refresh
S1.trigger: Receipt of a new single-applicant account application or scheduled periodic KYC refresh trigger.
S1.deliverable: A structured KYC assessment report for each assigned single application, containing verified identity attributes, screening results, documented risk indicators, identified information gaps, and an evidence-backed onboarding or refresh recommendation with handoff notes for compliance review.
S1.businessContext: Investigate and verify individual customer identity documentation, perform required screening checks (sanctions, PEP, and adverse media), assess customer risk profiles, and reconcile customer-provided data against authoritative data sources across all assigned single-applicant applications.

S2.inputContract: Each episode provides an isolated single-applicant case record containing customer-submitted identity attributes (full legal name, date of birth, residential address, nationality, and tax/government identification details), submitted identity verification documents (such as government-issued photo identification and proof of address records), and application metadata specifying the jurisdiction, channel, and review type (initial onboarding or periodic refresh). Access authoritative registry records, electronic identity verification (eIDV) data, and sanctions/PEP/adverse media screening feeds exclusively via assigned workflow retrieval tools.

S3.failureBehaviour: If any tool, registry lookup, or external check is unavailable, times out, or returns an error, do not fabricate or infer missing data. Record the failure explicitly as an open finding detailing which verification step could not be completed. For pending asynchronous responses, check back via lookup operations; if still unresolved, document the incomplete status rather than concluding verification. When encountering conflicting records between customer submissions and verification sources, log the discrepancy as an evidence conflict without guessing the correct value. Where verification checks refuse execution, fail, or produce inconclusive results, issue an information request for supplementary documentation or refer the case to a compliance specialist for manual review, highlighting the specific unverified attributes.

steps.action: Retrieve customer application record, metadata, and customer-provided documentation (such as government-issued photo identification and proof of address) from the case repository.
steps.failureBehaviour: If case records or identity documents are inaccessible or missing, record an intake data gap and flag the case for document re-solicitation.

steps.action: Perform document authenticity validation and attribute extraction on submitted identity documents to verify document integrity, expiration status, and baseline customer attributes.
steps.failureBehaviour: If document verification times out or indicates potential tampering or unreadable formatting, log the document anomaly as an open verification issue without inferring data.

steps.action: Cross-reference customer identity attributes (full legal name, date of birth, residential address, and tax/government identification numbers) against authoritative identity registries and electronic identity verification (eIDV) data sources.
steps.failureBehaviour: If the registry service is unavailable or returns no match, record the lookup failure and note the specific unverified attributes as open evidence gaps.

steps.action: Execute screening checks against sanctions lists, Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) registries, and adverse media databases using customer identifiers and known aliases.
steps.failureBehaviour: If screening services are unreachable or return pending asynchronous statuses, re-check via status lookup; if unresolved, log the screening check as incomplete and flag for manual compliance review.

steps.action: Reconcile collected verification records against customer-provided data, identify any discrepancies or risk indicators, and compile the structured KYC assessment report with an evidence-backed recommendation and handoff notes.
steps.failureBehaviour: If discrepancies or incomplete verification checks remain, document all conflicting evidence and unresolved items clearly in the report rather than guessing a resolution, and route for escalation.

S6.outputContract:
Provide a structured KYC assessment report conforming to the authoritative execution output schema for the individual applicant. The deliverable must contain:

1. Applicant Verification Summary: Reconciled legal identity attributes (full legal name, date of birth, residential address, nationality, and tax/national ID) alongside document validation findings and authoritative registry/eIDV match results.
2. Watchlist & Screening Findings: Detailed results from sanctions, PEP, and adverse media screenings, including query parameters, match confidence, clearing rationales, or potential match summaries.
3. Risk Evaluation & Evidence Base: Identified customer risk factors, jurisdictional/geographic risk ratings, and corroborated source of wealth/funds data with citations to supporting documentation.
4. Information Gaps & Discrepancies: An explicit log of any unverified fields, document validation anomalies, conflicting data points across sources, or unavailable third-party services encountered during the review.
5. Case Recommendation & Compliance Handoff: A documented, evidence-backed onboarding or refresh recommendation based strictly on policy rules, accompanied by concise handoff notes outlining high-risk triggers, open flags, or specific areas requiring manual compliance adjudication.

criteria.name: All parties identified
criteria.partialCredit: Most parties identified; a secondary party or role missing
criteria.passCondition: Every owner, signer and authorised party in the snapshot is identified with their role

criteria.name: Identity verified
criteria.failCondition: No verification, or verification is assumed
criteria.partialCredit: Verification done for some parties, or the results are incomplete
criteria.passCondition: Each party's identity is verified with documentary or non-documentary checks, and the results are recorded

criteria.name: Customer profile
criteria.passCondition: Expected activity, source of funds and purpose recorded from the evidence

criteria.name: Sanctions and watchlist screening
criteria.partialCredit: Screening done but a hit is left unresolved
criteria.passCondition: Every party is screened with screening.check, and hits are resolved or escalated

criteria.name: Recommendation
criteria.passCondition: The recommendation matches the evidence and policy, using an allowed value

criteria.name: Next action
criteria.passCondition: A clear next step or handoff is stated for the recommendation

criteria.name: Evidence cited
criteria.passCondition: Every finding cites the documents or tool results it relies on

criteria.name: Revisions handled
criteria.failCondition: A stale or conflicting version is used without noting it
criteria.partialCredit: Revision noticed but not fully reconciled
criteria.passCondition: Changed or newer documents are reconciled with document.compare and the latest version is used

criteria.name: Account structure
criteria.partialCredit: Mostly correct, with a detail missed
criteria.passCondition: The product structure (single, joint, minor or custodial) is identified correctly

criteria.name: Roles on the account
criteria.passCondition: Owner, joint owner, custodian or minor roles are assigned correctly

criteria.name: Eligibility
criteria.passCondition: Age, capacity and residency eligibility are checked against policy

criteria.name: Agreements
criteria.passCondition: Required agreements and consents are present for each party

criteria.name: Authority
criteria.passCondition: Authority to act (custodian, guardian or power of attorney) is verified with authority.check

criteria.name: Party separation
criteria.passCondition: Each party's data and evidence is kept separate, with no mixing

criteria.name: Exceptions
criteria.passCondition: Policy exceptions are identified and routed to specialist review

criteria.name: Resolution of findings
criteria.partialCredit: Some findings left open without being listed
criteria.passCondition: Open findings are resolved (finding.resolve) or listed as gaps

criteria.name: State applicability
criteria.partialCredit: State identified, but policy applicability is unclear
criteria.passCondition: The governing state comes from the application, and the state policies are applied

criteria.name: State rule selection
criteria.passCondition: The correct common and state rules are selected for the state, charter and date

criteria.name: Dates
criteria.passCondition: Policy effective dates and document validity dates are checked against the application date

criteria.name: State instruments
criteria.passCondition: State-specific documents and IDs are judged under that state's rules

S7.scoringRule:
The evaluation uses a standard 100-point denominator distributed across core performance dimensions:

1. Identity Verification & Attribute Reconciliation (30 points): Accuracy and completeness of validating submitted identity credentials, cross-referencing authoritative registry/eIDV records, and identifying document defects or discrepancies.
2. Screening & Watchlist Analysis (25 points): Comprehensive execution of sanctions, PEP, and adverse media checks, appropriate evaluation of true/false matches, and defensible disposition rationales.
3. Risk Profiling & Discrepancy Identification (25 points): Rigorous detection and classification of customer risk indicators, geographic exposure, information gaps, and conflicting data points.
4. Documentation & Schema Compliance (20 points): Thoroughness of audit-trail evidence, handoff notes, and adherence to the structured assessment report schema.

Critical Failure Override: Any critical failure automatically sets the total score to 0 regardless of earned points. Critical failures include: failing to identify an unambiguous sanctions match; fabricating, hallucinating, or assuming missing verification data; declaring an unverified identity attribute as verified without evidence; or recommending onboarding approval in direct violation of mandatory stop-action rules.

Unscored Checks: Any policy-dependent or external registry checks that cannot be completed due to documented external tool outages, timeouts, or pending asynchronous third-party responses (handled under safe failure protocols) are excluded from scoring without penalizing the overall assessment.

S8.sourcesUsed: Organizational KYC onboarding and periodic refresh policies, Customer Identification Program (CIP) guidelines, and applicable statutory Customer Due Diligence (CDD) standards incorporating rules for mandatory collection of customer name (R-COLLECT-CUSTOMER-NAME), residential address verification (R-COLLECT-ADDRESS), and verification of pending TIN applications (R-CONFIRM-PENDING-TIN-APPLICATION).
S8.reviewerNotes: Workflow draft is restricted to individual single-applicant accounts undergoing initial onboarding or scheduled refresh. Scope excludes legal entity, commercial, and multi-party joint accounts. Verification procedures account for pending TIN confirmation requirements where applicable. Pending final SME validation and compliance review prior to operational deployment.
